You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
The one who practices sin is of the devil, because the devil has been sinning from the very start. This is why the Son of God was revealed, to destroy the works of the devil.

notes.quote: οὐκ ἐγὼ ὑμᾶς τοὺς δώδεκα ἐξελεξάμην, καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν εἷς διάβολός ἐστιν
notes.note: Jesus gives this remark in the form of a question in order to emphasize that one of the twelve disciples will betray him. Alternate translation: [I chose you, the Twelve, myself, and one of you is a devil!]
See how you translated the Twelve in verse 67.

The word devil could mean: (1) one of Jesus’ twelve disciples was a wicked person whose thoughts and actions resembled those of the devil or was being influenced or controlled by the devil. It does not mean that this person actually was the devil in human form. It also does not imply that there is more than one devil. Alternate translation: [one of you is wicked like the devil] or [one of you is controlled by the devil]; (2) one of Jesus’ twelve disciples was speaking harmful and untrue things about Jesus to others. This meaning is possible because the word translated as devil can also mean “slanderer.” Alternate translation: [one of you is a slanderer]

verses.text: He was speaking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. For although Judas was one of the Twelve, he was later to betray Jesus.

xrefs.text: Then one of the Twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests

For certain men have crept in among you unnoticed— ungodly ones who were designated long ago for condemnation. They turn the grace of our God into a license for immorality, and they deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.
“Brothers, the Scripture had to be fulfilled that the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became a guide for those who arrested Jesus.
Even my close friend whom I trusted, the one who shared my bread, has lifted up his heel against me.
But it is you, a man like myself, my companion and close friend.
Now Judas His betrayer also knew the place, because Jesus had often met there with His disciples.
Jesus answered, “It is the one to whom I give this morsel after I have dipped it. Then He dipped the morsel and gave it to Judas son of Simon Iscariot.
He was delivered up by God’s set plan and foreknowledge, and you, by the hands of the lawless, put Him to death by nailing Him to the cross.

notes.note: In this verse John provides background information about what Jesus said in the previous verse. Use the natural form in your language for expressing background information.
Judas and Simon are names of two men. This Simon is not the same as Simon Peter. Iscariot is a distinguishing term that most likely means he came from the village of Kerioth.
